name: Cocoanut Pudding
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: ½ cup stale sponge cake, crumbed fine
ingredients.originalText: ½ cup stale sponge cake, crumbed fine

ingredients.name: large cup rich milk—cream, if you can get it
ingredients.originalText: 1 large cup rich milk—cream, if you can get it

instructions.text: Cream the butter and sugar, and add the beaten yolks.
When these are well mixed, put in the cocoanut; stir well before adding the milk, cake-crumbs, flavoring; and lastly, the whites of three eggs.

Whip the other whites stiff with three tablespoonfuls of powdered sugar; flavor with vanilla, and just before taking the pudding from the oven, spread this méringue over the top, and close the oven until the icing is slightly browned.
Bake in all three-quarters of an hour.

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Cream the butter and sugar, and add the beaten yolks.
2. When these are well mixed, put in the cocoanut; stir well before adding the milk, cake-crumbs, flavoring; and lastly, the whites of three eggs.
3. Whip the other whites stiff with three tablespoonfuls of powdered sugar; flavor with vanilla, and just before taking the pudding from the oven, spread this méringue over the top, and close the oven until the icing is slightly browned.
4. Bake in all three-quarters of an hour.
